mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5%, it signals a tight labor market that supports strong consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 4.5%, or the Rank IC for this signal is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1200 and retail sales (RSAFS) above 450,000 million dollars indicates robust consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST>1200 and RSAFS>450000) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative coefficient with p>0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During recessionary phases, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) relative to the prior month signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when INDPRO declines is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is above -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 150,000 thousand persons per month indicates strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when PAYEMS > 150,000 is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that may prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY, or the Rank IC for this signal is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening monetary policy amid a strong labor market, which typically leads to negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy faces a 'twin shock'.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with strong labor market
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25pp and UNRATE decline > 0.1pp) fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a positive coefficient with p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1150 thousand units signals a cooling housing market and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when HOUST < 1150 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is above -0.03.
